    Splitting a point into a receiver and an emitter #

    Let 1 = e₁ + e_z + e₂ be orthogonal idempotents of B such that, writing e_j B e_i for the morphisms i → j, there is no morphism between the parts 1 and 2, none from z to 1 and none from 2 to z, and e_z B e_z = k e_z. Then every module is the direct sum of e₁U + X and e₂U + Y, where X ⊆ e_z U is killed by e₂ B e_z and Y is a complement. So an indecomposable module is killed by e_z B e₁ or by e₂ B e_z, and a minimal representation-infinite algebra admits no such splitting with both blocks nonzero (IsMinimalRepInfinite.not_split). This replaces the emitter-receiver splitting used by Bongartz ([mild] §4, [Standard] §3).
